svg.title: Norwegian Atlantic Slope Current: separately scoped reported dimensions
svg.desc: A source-reported approximate3500kilometre broad historical eastern-branch extent. Six local width records retain distinct definitions:30to50kilometre regional summary,50kilometre surface branch scale,25to30kilometre relative-geostrophic span two50kilometre static mean-core extents and one40kilometre contextual mean-flow width. These are not six independent new observations, a mapped axis, a whole-current width or a seasonal range.

g.text: Norwegian Atlantic Slope Current · source reports
Orvik and Skagseth (2003), introduction [3]; not a dated or modern regional axis.
Includes downstream context now named West Spitsbergen; lengths are not additive.
30–50 km · cited regional branch-width summary (Orvik et al., 2001)
≈ 50 km · surface branch scale (Mork and Skagseth, 2010)
25–30 km · Gimsøy relative-geostrophic span (Fer et al., 2020)
≈ 50 km · Svinøy static mean core, 50 m plane (Baumann et al., 2026)
≈ 50 km · Gimsøy static mean-core extent (Baumann et al., 2026)
≈ 40 km · Svinøy mean-flow description (Orvik and Skagseth, 2003)
Distinct from Norwegian Current, Norwegian Coastal Current and western frontal branch.
No paired geographic edges, annual range, whole-current width or physical state join.
Historical proposal records remain traceable; six records are not six new observations.
Original OSW scalar summary · primary source links and definitions in the working admission
